title: Next.js Web Development
description: Beginner-to-advanced Next.js App Router reference covering routing, Server and Client Components, data and cache behavior, mutations, Route Handlers, metadata, errors, security, performance, testing, and deployment.

sections.title: App Router & Project Structure
sections.description: Use file conventions to define route segments, layouts, loading, errors, and APIs.

subtopics.title: Pages, Layouts & Route Segments
subtopics.description: Folders define URL segments; page exposes a route; layouts wrap descendants and preserve state across client navigation.

codeBlocks.code:
app/
  layout.tsx                 root HTML/body layout
  page.tsx                   /
  dashboard/
    layout.tsx               shared dashboard shell
    page.tsx                 /dashboard
    loading.tsx              streaming fallback
    error.tsx                client error boundary
    not-found.tsx            segment not-found UI
  api/health/route.ts        Route Handler

callouts.title: Layouts Do Not Receive Route URL
callouts.text: Shared layouts may be cached and do not re-render on navigation. Use appropriate client navigation hooks in a small Client Component when pathname-dependent UI is required.

subtopics.title: Dynamic, Catch-All, Groups & Parallel Routes
subtopics.description: Dynamic folders capture parameters; groups organize without URL segments; parallel slots render independently; intercepting routes overlay navigation contexts.

codeBlocks.code:
app/products/[productId]/page.tsx      /products/42
app/docs/[...slug]/page.tsx              /docs/a/b
app/shop/[[...filters]]/page.tsx         optional catch-all
app/(marketing)/about/page.tsx           /about
app/dashboard/@analytics/page.tsx        parallel slot
app/@modal/(.)products/[id]/page.tsx     intercepted modal route

callouts.title: Complex Routing Needs Direct-Load Tests
callouts.text: Test client navigation, refresh/direct URL, back/forward, missing slot defaults, deep links, and unauthorized states. Interception must degrade correctly without navigation history.

subtopics.title: Linking, Prefetching & Programmatic Navigation
subtopics.description: Use Link for navigation; it supports client transitions and prefetching. Use next/navigation hooks only in Client Components when imperative behavior is required.

callouts.title: Never Push Untrusted URLs
callouts.text: Validate/allowlist navigation targets. Unsafe schemes supplied to router APIs can execute in page context; prefer constructed internal routes.

sections.title: Server & Client Components
sections.description: Keep server capabilities on the server and minimize client bundle boundaries.

subtopics.title: Server Components by Default
subtopics.description: Pages and layouts are Server Components by default. They may await data, access server resources, and send rendered output/RSC payload without shipping their component code to browsers.

table.title: Server and Client Component Boundaries
rows: No; requires a use client boundary
Use state, effects, or browser APIs
May pass Client Components as children or imports
May receive rendered Server Component content through composition

callouts.title: Server Does Not Mean Secret Automatically
callouts.text: Data passed to Client Components or rendered HTML reaches the browser. Select safe fields and use server-only boundaries for modules containing credentials.

subtopics.title: use client Boundaries
subtopics.description: Client Components are needed for state, effects, event handlers, browser APIs, and client-only libraries. The directive marks a module-graph boundary.

callouts.title: Push Boundaries Down
callouts.text: Do not mark an entire layout client-side for one interactive widget. Isolate the widget so static/server-rendered parents and dependencies stay outside the client bundle.

subtopics.title: Server/Client Composition & Serialization
subtopics.description: Server Components may be passed as children/props into Client Components. Props crossing the boundary must be serializable by the React transport.

callouts.title: Do Not Pass Rich Server Objects
callouts.text: Database clients, class instances, request objects, functions (except supported server functions), and secrets do not belong in Client Component props. Map to explicit serializable DTOs.

sections.title: Data, Caching & Streaming
sections.description: Make freshness, request memoization, persistent caching, and invalidation intentional.

subtopics.title: Fetching in Server Components
subtopics.description: Fetch data near the component that needs it; use Promise concurrency to avoid waterfalls and React cache for request-scoped function memoization where suitable.

callouts.title: Parallelize Independent Work
callouts.text: Starting one request only after another awaits creates server waterfalls. Preserve dependency ordering only when the second operation needs the first result.

subtopics.title: Cache Components & use cache
subtopics.description: When Cache Components is enabled, use cache marks functions/components/routes cacheable; cacheLife and cacheTag define lifetime and invalidation groups.

callouts.title: Cache Semantics Are Version-Sensitive
callouts.text: Cache Components is opt-in in current guidance. Pin Next.js, follow the matching version docs, and test authenticated/runtime request data outside shared cache scopes.

subtopics.title: Invalidation, Suspense & Streaming
subtopics.description: Invalidate affected paths/tags after mutations. Suspense boundaries stream independent fallbacks and prevent one slow region from delaying the whole route.

callouts.title: Invalidation Must Match Writes
callouts.text: Missing invalidation serves stale data; overly broad invalidation destroys cache value. Define ownership and tags alongside the mutation, not as an afterthought.

sections.title: Server Functions, Forms & Route Handlers
sections.description: Validate, authorize, mutate, and invalidate on the server boundary.

subtopics.title: Server Actions & Form Mutations
subtopics.description: A use server function executes on the server and can be bound to form actions. Treat every invocation as an externally reachable mutation endpoint.

callouts.title: Authenticate and Authorize Inside Every Action
callouts.text: UI visibility is not authorization. Validate input, verify resource ownership/role, protect origin/CSRF assumptions, limit payloads, and avoid returning sensitive errors.

subtopics.title: useActionState, Pending & Optimistic UI
subtopics.description: Client form hooks surface pending/result state; optimistic updates improve latency perception but must reconcile with the authoritative server outcome.

callouts.title: Return Expected Errors as Data
callouts.text: Validation and conflict errors should become structured action state. Throw unexpected failures for error boundaries/telemetry without exposing stack or internal detail.

subtopics.title: Route Handlers
subtopics.description: route.ts exports HTTP method handlers using Request/Response APIs. Use for webhooks, public APIs, non-HTML responses, and backend-for-frontend endpoints.

callouts.title: Webhooks Need Raw Bytes and Idempotency
callouts.text: Verify signatures before trusting parsed data, reject replay where supported, store delivery IDs, and respond within provider deadlines.

sections.title: Metadata, Assets & Error UX
sections.description: Use framework primitives for discoverability, media performance, and failure boundaries.

subtopics.title: Metadata, Sitemap & Social Images
subtopics.description: Export static metadata or generateMetadata for route-specific values; use file conventions for icons, robots, sitemap, and generated social images.

callouts.title: Validate Canonical URLs
callouts.text: Build URLs from trusted base/config and normalized route parameters. Avoid indexing private, duplicate, filtered, or error pages unintentionally.

subtopics.title: Image, Font & Script Optimization
subtopics.description: next/image manages responsive sizing/loading; next/font self-hosts optimized fonts; next/script controls third-party execution strategy.

codeBlocks.code:
<Image
  src={product.imageUrl}
  alt={product.imageAlt}
  width={800}
  height={600}
  sizes="(max-width: 768px) 100vw, 50vw"
/>

callouts.title: Remote Images Need Policy
callouts.text: Restrict remote patterns, preserve aspect ratios, provide meaningful alt text, and do not mark many images priority/preload; it can hurt the critical path.

subtopics.title: loading, error, global-error & not-found
subtopics.description: Segment files provide streaming fallback, client error recovery, root failure UI, and 404 handling. Expected domain absence can call notFound.

callouts.title: Log Server and Client Failures
callouts.text: Error UIs need safe messages and correlation IDs. Capture original errors in server/client telemetry without exposing stack traces or secrets.

sections.title: Security, Runtime & Deployment
sections.description: Keep trust boundaries explicit across server, browser, edge, cache, and infrastructure.

subtopics.title: Authentication, Authorization & Proxy
subtopics.description: Use optimistic route gating only for UX. Perform secure authorization near data access and mutations; central request interception should remain lightweight.

codeBlocks.code:
Authentication: establish identity from secure session/token
Authorization: verify action + resource on every server operation
Proxy/middleware: redirects, headers, coarse checks; avoid slow data access
Server Component: safe display gating, not sole mutation protection
Action/Route Handler/data layer: authoritative validation and authorization

callouts.title: Cache and Identity Must Not Mix Accidentally
callouts.text: Never place user-specific data in a shared cache without identity-scoped keys and correct privacy semantics. Read cookies/headers outside shared cache scopes.

subtopics.title: Node, Edge & Environment Variables
subtopics.description: Choose runtime per dependency and platform capability. Server environment stays private unless explicitly exposed with the public prefix/build mechanism.

callouts.title: Edge Is a Different Runtime
callouts.text: Node built-ins, native packages, filesystem, sockets, execution limits, and connection behavior differ. Test the actual target and prefer Node unless edge placement brings measured value.

subtopics.title: Deployment, Instrumentation & Standalone Output
subtopics.description: Deployment must provide build/runtime configuration, cache storage semantics, image optimization, logging/tracing, graceful shutdown, and durable external state.

callouts.title: Local Memory Is Per Instance
callouts.text: Do not rely on module globals or local filesystem for shared sessions, jobs, uploads, or durable cache across serverless/container replicas.

sections.title: Performance, Testing & Checklist
sections.description: Measure server, client, cache, network, and deployment behavior together.

subtopics.title: Bundle, Rendering & Data Performance
subtopics.description: Reduce client boundaries, avoid sequential data waterfalls, stream slow regions, cache intentionally, and inspect real route/client bundle output.

codeBlocks.code:
Server cost: database/API latency, concurrency, cache hit rate, cold start
Network: TTFB, streaming, CDN, image/font/script delivery
Client: shipped JS, hydration, long tasks, interaction latency
Navigation: prefetch usefulness, RSC payload, dynamic route latency
Correctness: stale data, invalidation fan-out, user cache isolation

callouts.title: Server Components Are Not Free
callouts.text: They reduce client JavaScript but still consume server/data resources and produce payload. Profile database queries, serialization, cache, and streamed response timing.

subtopics.title: Unit, Component & End-to-End Testing
subtopics.description: Unit-test domain/server functions, component-test interactive Client Components, and use end-to-end tests for routing, RSC, actions, cookies, caching, and deployment behavior.

codeBlocks.code:
Unit: validation, authorization policy, cache-key logic, data mapping
Component: forms, pending/error states, accessibility
Integration: Route Handlers/actions with test database and identity
E2E: direct URL + client navigation, auth redirects, mutation + revalidation, error/not-found
Production smoke: built output behind real proxy/CDN/runtime

callouts.title: Mocking RSC Internals Is Low Value
callouts.text: Test pure server logic separately and verify framework composition with integration/E2E tests. Avoid brittle assertions on internal payload or cache implementation.

subtopics.title: Production Checklist
subtopics.description: Review boundaries, freshness, authorization, resilience, metadata, and deployed behavior.

codeBlocks.code:
□ Server Components are default; client boundaries are minimal
□ Cross-boundary props are safe and serializable
□ Independent data requests run concurrently
□ Cache lifetime/tags and mutation invalidation are documented
□ User-specific data cannot enter shared caches
□ Every action/handler validates and authorizes
□ Loading, error, not-found, retry, and no-JS form behavior work
□ Dynamic/parallel/intercepted routes work on direct load and Back
□ Metadata, canonical URLs, images, fonts, and scripts are correct
□ Node/Edge choice matches dependencies
□ Durable state is external to instances
□ Client bundle, server latency, cache hit rate, and Web Vitals are measured
□ Built deployment is tested behind the real host/proxy/CDN
